_how_to_edit: The story page, replay map and home hero read this file on every load. Edit it, run `node groundstop/src/build.js`, commit and push to main; no Squarespace edit is needed. Times are hours on an Eastern clock on Nov. 13, 2026 (17.5 = 5:30 p.m.; values past 24 mean Nov. 14). Set lift to null while the stop is in effect.
headline_status: The ground stop is still in effect, and major airlines may stop flying for the night
cause: Telecommunications outage at air traffic control
moments: A Friday afternoon, with flights departing on schedule across the country.
About 3:10 p.m.
Flights bound for Chicago O’Hare are stopped over communications problems, and Midway follows three minutes later.
Nationwide ground stop. More than 3,100 flights already in the air are allowed to continue to their destinations.
The transportation secretary says a communication issue is affecting air route traffic control centers.
The FAA advisory now runs to 11:30 p.m. Eastern, and no end time is confirmed.
About 5:15 p.m.
The FAA says a temporary telecommunications outage caused the stop, and officials say they see no sign of an attack.
About 6:00 p.m.
The FAA says the stop remains in effect and that flights will be released as each en route center recovers.
Fox Weather counts 598 commercial flights still in the air, down from more than 3,100 when the stop began.
About 7:10 p.m.
An airline source tells CNN that major airlines could shut down operations for the rest of the night.
The stop is 3 hours and 42 minutes old, and the homeland security secretary says there is no known time frame for a fix.
facts: Eastern start time, the only one of the three stops to begin after noon
flights in the air when the stop began, allowed to finish their trips
flights delayed by 6:30 p.m. Eastern, with more than 2,500 canceled, according to Fox Weather
unknown: What is not known. The FAA blames a temporary telecommunications outage but has not said publicly what caused it or when all departures will resume. An airline source told CNN that the FAA traced the problem to network routers and that it is believed to have started at Chicago Midway before spreading nationwide. This replay ends at 7:36 p.m. Eastern on Nov. 13, the last time we checked, with the stop still in effect and flights within Alaska and Hawaii and some overwater departures still allowed. Three days earlier, on Nov. 10, the agency expanded SMART, an AI tool that suggests flight reroutes, to all 22 centers. No official has connected the tool to the stop, and no reporting so far shows a link.
status_html: As of 7:36 p.m. Eastern on Friday the stop was still in effect, 3 hours and 42 minutes after it began. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there is no known time frame for resolving the outage, and an airline source told CNN at about 7:10 p.m. that major airlines could shut down operations for the rest of the night. The FAA said at about 6 p.m. that flights would be released as each en route center recovers, and the exceptions so far are narrow: flights within Alaska and Hawaii, West Coast flights to Hawaii, and some overwater departures from San Francisco and Boston. Fox Weather counted more than 10,500 delays and more than 2,500 cancellations by 6:30 p.m., up from 10,494 delays and 1,913 cancellations at 6:04 p.m., and 598 commercial flights were still in the air at 6:30 p.m., about one-fifth of the more than 3,100 airborne when the stop began.
compare_html: Friday's stop passed the length of the entire 2023 stop at about 5:24 p.m. and had run 222 minutes by 7:36 p.m., about two and a half times the roughly 90 minutes of 2023. It also began late on a Friday afternoon where the 2023 stop began early on a Wednesday, which leaves airlines little of the day to recover. The more than 2,500 cancellations counted by 6:30 p.m. were nearly double the 1,300-plus logged for the whole day in 2023, and the more than 10,500 delays had passed that day's roughly 10,000. The effects now reach into Saturday: the Big 12 told CNN it is evaluating changes to its football schedule because teams cannot travel.
notknown_html:
The FAA has not said publicly what caused the telecommunications outage. An airline source told CNN that the FAA told airlines the outages resulted from a problem with network routers, and that the problem is believed to have started at Chicago Midway and spread nationwide. CBS News reported that the affected system is operated by the contractor L3Harris, which had not responded to its request for comment. The FAA has confirmed neither account.

Mullin said there was no indication of a threat to the country, and the FAA said it does not believe the outage was a cyberattack. A senior security source told CNN late Friday that the FBI, the Department of Homeland Security and the National Security Agency had found no sign of an attack and that the search of the aviation system's network connections would continue for days.

Three days before the stop, on Nov. 10, the FAA expanded SMART, an AI tool that suggests flight reroutes, to all 22 centers. Mullin said the administration is examining that rollout, according to Fox News, and no official has connected the tool to the stop or reported a link so far.

This story reflects what was known at 7:36 p.m. Eastern on Nov. 13, 2026. We will update the end time, the cause and the final delay counts as the FAA and flight trackers report them.
